title: Strong converse for the quantum capacity of a general channel
source: Hayashi discusses the general strong-converse gap in Section~9.9.3, pp.~554--555, after presenting the Rains-information converse bound in Theorem~9.12 \sourcecite{ref:h13-book}{Hay17}. Tomamichel, Wilde, and Winter formulate the general question in their Introduction and distinguish the quantum capacity from its strong-converse capacity \sourcecite{ref:h13-tww}{TWW17}.
progress: The regularized coherent information determines the vanishing-error threshold $Q(\mathcal N)$ but does not imply Eq.~\eqref{eq:h13-converse}; see Hayashi's Theorem~9.10 and Section~9.9.3 \sourcecite{ref:h13-book}{Hay17}.

Tomamichel, Wilde, and Winter's Theorem~8 gives an exponential strong-converse upper bound using the regularized channel Rains information, even with classical pre- and post-processing. Their Section~VI proves equality with capacity for generalized dephasing channels. The general upper bound need not coincide with $Q(\mathcal N)$ \sourcecite{ref:h13-tww}{TWW17}.

Kondra, Brinster, Kampermann, Bru{\ss}, and Wyderka prove an all-code exponential strong converse for finite-dimensional antidegradable channels in Theorem~1 and degradable channels in Theorem~4 of their August~2026 preprint. This includes erasure channels over the full parameter range. Their Theorem~11 also covers a specified nondegradable multilevel amplitude-damping family. Their general-channel bound in Theorem~8 does not determine the capacity, as discussed in Section~VIII \sourcecite{ref:h13-kondra}{KBK+26}.

Tomamichel proves an exponential strong converse for Pauli channels within the class of stabilizer codes, with arbitrary decoders; see Section~6 of the July~2026 preprint. The restriction concerns the encoded subspace and cannot simply be removed. Section~8.3 identifies the remaining extension to unrestricted encoders \sourcecite{ref:h13-tomamichel}{Tom26}.

comment: Audited on 2026-09-09, including the full July and August~2026 preprints. Their subclass theorems leave the general-channel implication in Eq.~\eqref{eq:h13-converse} unresolved. This record asks for convergence to zero, without requiring an exponential rate. The solved degradable-channel record proves the stronger exponential statement for a subclass; the transpose-degradable record asks for an exponential converse in another restricted class. Rains-information achievability under an enlarged PPT assistance model is a separate operational question. In particular, the book's Rains-relative-entropy bound must not be identified with max-Rains information merely because it is named an SDP bound.
